ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the upper part is a fixed support; on the left side there is a fixed pulley, and block B is suspended from the lower end of the vertical rope segment on the left. After the rope passes around the fixed pulley on the left, it forms an inclined rope segment downward connected to the movable pulley at the lower right, and then from the other side of the movable pulley it is fixed obliquely upward to the upper support. Block A is suspended below the movable pulley through a vertical connection. The figure marks the angle between the inclined ropes on the two sides of the movable pulley as 60°. The system is stationary, and the masses of the rope and pulleys are neglected and there is no friction, so the tension everywhere in the same rope is equal, set as T. Reasoning: Block B is acted on only by gravity m_Bg and the vertically upward rope tension T. Static equilibrium gives m_Bg=T. Analyze the movable pulley and block A as a whole: the movable pulley is acted on by the pulls of two inclined rope segments, each with magnitude T. The angle between the two rope segments is 60°, and their resultant force is upward along the angle bisector, with magnitude 2Tcos30°=√3T. The whole is in static equilibrium, so the weight of A satisfies m_Ag=√3T. Dividing the two equations: m_A/m_B=(√3T/g)/(T/g)=√3. Therefore the mass ratio of blocks A and B is √3, which can also be written as A:B=√3:1.
